question: Should OpenClaw accept `currentTokenCount` plus these token-budget SDK helpers as a stable public ContextEngine/plugin SDK contract now, or fold token-budget metadata into the broader assemble metadata RFC?
rationale: The patch changes public plugin API and SDK exports that third-party context engines may compile against, while related assemble metadata design remains open and broader than this one field.

options.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Repairs
options.body: Approve `currentTokenCount` as a separate backward-compatible API, but require the two mechanical fixes and redacted live behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Fold Into Broader RFC
options.body: Pause this PR and land token counts together with the provenance/internal-event/live-turn assemble metadata design tracked in the related RFC.

options.title: Keep Helpers Private For Now
options.body: Allow internal token-count plumbing only and defer public SDK helper exports until the plugin API shape is maintainer-owned.

recommendation.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Repairs
recommendation.body: Approve `currentTokenCount` as a separate backward-compatible API, but require the two mechanical fixes and redacted live behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman is assigned and has the strongest recent merged history on the context-engine token-budget path affected by this API decision.
